newsitem.title: INDIA: Iranian minister to discuss Afghanistan in India.
newsitem.headline: Iranian minister to discuss Afghanistan in India.

text.p: Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati will visit New Delhi this week to discuss regional developments, including the fighting in Afghanistan, the Indian Foreign Ministry said on Tuesday.
Velayati was scheduled to arrive in the Indian capital on Wednesday for two days of hastily arranged talks, a ministry official said.
The talks would precede a visit by Indian Vice-President Kocheril Raman Narayanan to Iran starting on October 22.

The Foreign Ministry said in a statement at the weekend that it was following the fighting in Afghanistan with deep concern and that the fall of Kabul to Taleban militia had created "a dangerous new situation of great fluidity".
Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral was quoted on Tuesday as saying New Delhi continued to recognise the ousted government of Burhanuddin Rabbani.

Asked whether India was willing to recognise the Taleban, Gujral was quoted by The Hindu newspaper as saying: "India does not have preferences. It is for the people of Afghanistan to decide. India does not support direct or indirect intervention."

In the weekend statement, the Foreign Ministry said it was shocked by the "brutal murder" of former president Najibullah, and that "the imposition of a harsh and fundamentalist ideology...has raised misgivings about the human rights situation".
India supports efforts by United Nations Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali and his special representative to bring peace to Afghanistan, the statement said.
